question:
Create a new KiCad project named b38 in the project directory and draw its schematic for the following request.

Build the through-hole ATmega328 DIP-28 DRAM tester with a crystal clock, parallel DIP-20 ZIF and ZIP-20 514256-style sockets, a three-option DIP switch, reset button and standard ICSP. Firmware uses PD0-PD7 for A0-A7, PB4 for A8, PC0-PC3 for I/O1-I/O4 and PB0/PB1/PB2/PB3 for nCAS/nRAS/nOE/nWE. Fit individual 47 ohm series resistors on address, data and control lines. PC4 connects directly to the ZIP reserved contact and through 47 ohms to the DIP reserved contact; ICSP MOSI is tapped on the socket side of the nWE resistor.
The three DIP-switch options pull socket-side A2, A3 and the PC5/socket-power node high, each with a 1M pull-down. Include a common-anode dual result LED, with 2N7000 low-side drivers on MISO and SCK and 100/150 ohm LED resistors. Power comes from a two-contact Micro-USB power-only interface through a 0.5 A polyfuse. Include reset and crystal support, supply bypassing and bulk capacitance. Use socket symbols with the standard 514256 DIP/ZIP signal pinouts; there is no display connector in this version.
If socket symbols are unavailable, define labeled connectors with these pin orders. DIP pins 1-20: I/O1, I/O2, nWE, nRAS, reserved, A0, A1, A2, A3, VCC, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8, nOE, nCAS, I/O3, I/O4, GND. ZIP pins 1-20: nOE, nCAS, I/O3, I/O4, GND, I/O1, I/O2, nWE, nRAS, reserved, A0, A1, A2, A3, VCC, A4, A5, A6, A7, A8.
Local dependencies: No project-local libraries are supplied. Use standard KiCad parts where available; define missing module/connector symbols from the interfaces specified above.
answer:

The netlist was checked against the requested pin mapping, socket connections, switches, LED drivers and ICSP tap. ERC reports **0 errors and 3 warnings**: the three project-local symbols differ from their library copies, even after a refresh.

**Before building:**
- PC5 directly powers the sockets as requested, but may not safely supply the DRAM or capacitor inrush current. The 0.5 A fuse does not protect the GPIO.
- Firmware must prevent A2/A3 from driving low when their switches pull high, and must not drive PC5 low when socket power is switched on.
- The DIP, ZIP and two-contact USB interface symbols were created locally. Check their pinouts against the selected hardware; their footprints remain unassigned.
- The design assumes a 16 MHz crystal and compatible clock fuses. Check crystal loading and LED current ratings; the 100 Ω branch can draw roughly 30 mA with a 2 V LED.
